paraphrase: He describes a Cornell linguistics PhD and earlier work on Dravidian and Indo-European languages.

paraphrase: Most inscriptions are read right to left; seals and impressions require distinguishing the mirrored face.
offered_evidence: A seal and its mirrored impression are compared; he uses the impression as the canonical right-to-left display. The grounds for direction are left largely unstated.
note: All sounds/meanings in this ledger are Bonta’s proposals.

paraphrase: Patterned texts have recurring ordered fields; complex texts contain more variable, language-like sequences.
offered_evidence: Repeated sign classes, junctures, substitutions and positional restrictions.
note: All sounds/meanings in this ledger are Bonta’s proposals.
page_locator_basis: Unfoliated PDF; one-based physical leaf, verified against page-text segment index + 1.

paraphrase: He distinguishes transcriptive writing from notational writing and treats both as present in Indus texts.
offered_evidence: English weights, prices, dates and mathematical formulas illustrate abbreviation, changed spoken order and mixed notation. He announces application to Harappan texts at 0:59:44.
note: All sounds/meanings in this ledger are Bonta’s proposals.

paraphrase: Reading-order fields are P, M, C and T, with optional omissions. P is a position label rather than a grammatical prefix.
offered_evidence: Illustrated sequences show P–M–C–T and missing fields; P is explained as a positional convenience at 0:39:16.
note: All sounds/meanings in this ledger are Bonta’s proposals.

paraphrase: His M-field model has three optional components: an oval subfield, a fish subfield and an MS pair of a container with a central stick beside three long bars.
offered_evidence: Illustrated recurrent clusters.
note: All sounds/meanings in this ledger are Bonta’s proposals.

paraphrase: Within a complete M field, the reading order is oval, fish, MS.
offered_evidence: Repeated complete fields; manuscript explicitly reverses its printed left-to-right display.
note: All sounds/meanings in this ledger are Bonta’s proposals.

paraphrase: The fish subfield uses seven entries, has at most three entries and does not repeat an entry.
offered_evidence: Selected sequences and a proposed compound-sign treatment of fish with paired strokes.
note: All sounds/meanings in this ledger are Bonta’s proposals.

paraphrase: The oval subfield has at most two non-repeating members of a three-sign inventory.

paraphrase: The manuscript treats noun compounding as relatively rare in Dravidian and much more extensive in Sanskrit.

paraphrase: He categorically says attested Dravidian lacks noun compounding, while allowing that a Harappan-period ancestor could have had it. The paper makes a weaker comparison about extensive multi-noun name compounds.

paraphrase: He identifies Indo-Aryan as the most likely language from inferred compounding, affix behavior and proposed lexical readings.

paraphrase: He reads the MS construction as ma-tra and proposes matra, a measure or amount.

paraphrase: He obtains the proposed PU/bhu value by intersecting words ending in dhana, ma and pala, then requiring that the shared initial element also be common as a final or suffix element.

quotation: nothing that was not readable, nothing that that contradicted my results

paraphrase: An ICIT-first label generally means it was first encountered there, but can instead signal a more accurate transcription.
